name: Bright mauve
lede: Bright mauve is a dusty pink-purple whose Japanese library name, Benifuji, means "red wisteria," and it reads only about 4 units from plain [[mauve]] itself.

sections.title: Benifuji, red wisteria
sections.body:
Our library lists this color from the Wikipedia survey "Traditional colors of Japan," under the romanized name Benifuji, written 紅藤 [1]. The kanji combine 紅 (crimson, or a safflower red) with 藤 (wisteria), and the library's own gloss reads "red wisteria" [1]. The books consulted here give no date or further story for the name, so anything past that gloss would be unsupported [1].

The nearest already-named color in our library is [[mauve]], at a color-distance of 4.4 by the CIEDE2000 formula, close enough that most eyes would not tell them apart side by side [1]. The hex given here, #BB7796, is a modern screen approximation chosen to fit that gloss, not a measured dye [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color within range of this swatch is rare in our archive: it turns up in only 6 of the 23,781 paintings, about 0.03 percent, as photographed, rarer than 86 percent of the named colors we track [2]. The sample is too small here for century or role statistics [2]. As always, these are museum photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a match is a screen color, not a pigment test [2].
